When performing radiographic evaluation, which condition is best assessed using alternating
single-leg-stance x-rays? Answer Choices: (A) Piriformis syndrome (B) Labral tear ### Input **Original
Question:** A 43-year-old woman presents with a 2-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion,
fatigue, and lower extremity edema. She has no significant past medical history and takes no
medications. Physical examination reveals jugular venous distention, a right ventricular heave, and a
loud P2 component of the second heart sound. Echocardiogram shows right ventricular hypertrophy
and dilatation with normal left ventricular function. Right heart catheterization reveals a mean
pulmonary artery pressure of 55 mmHg. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? (C) Lumbar
radiculopathy (D) Sacroiliac joint dysfunction (E) Lumbosacral instability (F) Femoral neck stress
fracture (G) Pelvic ring instability (H) Femoroacetabular impingement (I) Acetabular dysplasia (J) Hip
abductor weakness
 A. Hip abductor weakness
B. Sacroiliac joint dysfunction
C. Piriformis syndrome
D. Lumbosacral instability
E. Acetabular dysplasia
F. Lumbar radiculopathy
G. Pelvic ring instability
H. Labral tear ### Input **Original Question:** A 45-year-old woman presents with a 2-month history
